stem.text: A particle moves along the x-axis so that its position at time t hours is \( x(t) = - 2 \left(t - 4\right) \left(t - 3\right)^{2} \), for \( 0 \le t \le 7 \). Find all open intervals of time in \( 0 < t < 7 \) during which the particle is moving to the left. Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: The particle is moving to the left exactly on \( \left(0, 3\right) \) and \( \left(\frac{11}{3}, 7\right) \), because \( v(t) < 0 \) there.

worked_solution.text: Differentiate the position with the product rule: \( v(t) = x'(t) = - 2 \left(t - 3\right) \left(3 t - 11\right) \).
worked_solution.rule_named: velocity is the derivative of position

worked_solution.text: Solving \( v(t) = 0 \) gives \( t = 3, \frac{11}{3} \), which split \( 0 < t < 7 \) into pieces on which v keeps one sign.

Testing a time in each piece shows \( v(t) < 0 \) exactly on \( \left(0, 3\right) \) and \( \left(\frac{11}{3}, 7\right) \). The particle moves to the left when its velocity is negative, so it moves to the left on \( \left(0, 3\right) \) and \( \left(\frac{11}{3}, 7\right) \).
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of velocity gives the direction of motion

options.label: The particle is moving to the left exactly on \( \left(0, 3\right) \) and \( \left(\frac{11}{3}, 7\right) \), because \( v(t) < 0 \) there.
The particle is moving to the left exactly on \( \left(4, 7\right) \), because \( x(t) < 0 \) there.
options.derivation: the direction read from the sign of the position x(t) rather than of the velocity

options.label: The particle is moving to the left exactly on \( \left(\frac{10}{3}, 7\right) \), because v(t) is decreasing there.
options.derivation: the direction read from whether the velocity is decreasing, the sign of its change, rather than from its sign

options.label: The particle is moving to the left exactly on \( \left(0, 3\right) \) and \( \left(3, 7\right) \), because \( v(t) < 0 \) there.
options.derivation: only the integer zero t = 3 found by trying whole-number times, so the zero at t = 11/3 is missed and each remaining piece is judged at one whole-number time
